per_option_rationale.rationale: The student adds (n+2) + (n+1) = 9 + 8 = 17 instead of multiplying the two consecutive factors.
The student cancels all terms and keeps only the last remaining factor n+2 = 9, missing that one full factor of (n+1) = 8 also survives the cancellation.
The student treats (n+2)! / n! as (n+1)! / n! = n+1 = 8, reducing the expression by one step too few and losing the (n+2) factor.

explanation: Cancel n! from numerator and denominator: (n+2)! / n! = (n+2) x (n+1) x n! / n! = (n+2)(n+1). With n = 7: 9 x 8 = 72.

explanation_sections.punchline: The answer is 72. Cancelling n! leaves exactly two uncancelled factors: (n+2) and (n+1). With n = 7 these are 9 and 8, whose product is 72.
explanation_sections.approach: Write out the factorial expansion just far enough to see what survives after cancellation. For k! / n! with k > n, exactly k - n factors remain: from n+1 up to k. Identify those factors first, then multiply.
explanation_sections.lesson: (n+r)! / n! = (n+r)(n+r-1)...(n+1). The number of surviving factors equals r. For r = 2 the result is always (n+1)(n+2), never a sum or a single term.
explanation_sections.timing: 75 seconds. Writing out the cancellation takes about 20 seconds. Multiplying two two-digit numbers takes under 15 seconds. If unsure, verify by computing 9! / 7! = (9 x 8 x 7!) / 7! directly.
